<thought>The proton NMR spectra show peaks at 1.20 ppm (doublet, 3H), 2.85 ppm (doublet, 2H), 3.09 ppm (quartet, 1H), 3.81 ppm (singlet, 3H), 7.15 ppm (doublet of doublets, 2H), and 7.92 ppm (doublet of doublets, 2H). The peaks at 7.15 and 7.92 ppm suggest aromatic protons, while the peaks at 1.20, 2.85, and 3.09 ppm suggest an aliphatic chain, possibly an isopropyl group. The singlet at 3.81 ppm could indicate a methoxy group. Combining this with the carbon NMR data, the compound might be an aromatic ester or ether. To confirm the structure, I should check the IR spectra for functional groups like carbonyls.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>

<thought>The IR spectra show a strong peak at 1739 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of a carbonyl group, likely an ester or ketone. The peaks around 3100-3000 cm⁻¹ suggest aromatic C-H stretching, supporting the presence of an aromatic ring. The combination of NMR and IR data suggests the compound could be an aromatic ester with an isopropyl group and a methoxy group. To narrow down the possibilities, I should search for similar structures in the NMRShift database using a potential SMILES string that fits these observations.</thought>
<action>search_by_smiles</action>
<action_input>{"smiles": "COC(=O)c1ccccc1C(C)C", "top_k": 5}</action_input>

<thought>The search results from the NMRShift database suggest that the SMILES string "COC(=O)c1ccccc1CC(C)=O" is a close match, with similar carbon NMR shifts. However, the presence of a carbonyl group at 205.7 ppm in the database entry indicates a ketone, which does not match our IR data showing a single carbonyl peak at 1739 cm⁻¹, more typical of an ester. The SMILES "COC(=O)c1ccccc1C(C)C" fits the NMR and IR data better, suggesting an aromatic ester with an isopropyl group and a methoxy group. I will validate this SMILES string to ensure it represents a valid chemical structure.</thought>
<action>validate_smiles</action>
<action_input>{"smiles": "COC(=O)c1ccccc1C(C)C"}</action_input>

<thought>The SMILES string "COC(=O)c1ccccc1C(C)C" is validated as a correct chemical structure. This structure is consistent with the NMR and IR data, indicating an aromatic ester with a methoxy group and an isopropyl group. Therefore, this is the most likely structure of the compound.</thought>
<final_answer>COC(=O)c1ccccc1C(C)C</final_answer>
